preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= N and 1 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= N for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:E+1])
preconditions.description: Every road in the input connects two distinct cities within the valid range [1, N].

preconditions.expression: E == len([line for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.strip()])
preconditions.description: The number of roads E exactly matches the number of input lines after the first line.
The first line contains exactly two integers N (number of cities) and E (number of roads).

preconditions.expression: all(a != b for a, b in [(int(line.split()[0]), int(line.split()[1])) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:E+1]])
preconditions.description: No road connects a city to itself.

preconditions.expression: len(set((int(line.split()[0]), int(line.split()[1])) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:E+1])) == E
preconditions.description: There are no duplicate roads in the same direction.

postconditions.description: If no solution exists, output is exactly 'NO'. Otherwise, output starts with 'YES' followed by exactly E lines, each representing a road's final orientation.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'YES' and all(line in [f'{a} {b}' for a, b in [(int(line.split()[0]), int(line.split()[1])) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:E+1]]] for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: If a solution exists, every output road (after 'YES') is a valid road from the original input, possibly with reversed direction.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'YES' and (lambda: all(any(all(visited[city] for city in range(1, N+1)) and len(visited) == E + 1 for visited in [set() for _ in range(N+1)]) for _ in range(N)))(stdout)
postconditions.description: If a solution exists, the output road network is Eulerian (i.e., for every city, there exists a cycle that traverses every road exactly once and visits every city). This is equivalent to the network being strongly connected and every city having equal in-degree and out-degree.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'NO' or (stdout.strip() == 'YES' and all(in_degree[city] == out_degree[city] for city in range(1, N+1)) and is_strongly_connected(adjacency_list))
postconditions.description: If a solution exists, the output road network must satisfy: (1) every city has equal in-degree and out-degree, and (2) the network is strongly connected. Here, `in_degree` and `out_degree` are computed from the output roads, and `is_strongly_connected` checks if there is a path between every pair of cities.
